title: Plan overlapping chunks
summary: Fixed-size chunking advances by a stride equal to the chunk size minus the overlap. Overlap protects a fact that would otherwise fall across a boundary, and it repeats work because the overlapping tokens are embedded twice.
example: 512-token chunks with 64 tokens of overlap advance 448 tokens at a time.
takeaway: The stride is chunk minus overlap, and the last chunk is short rather than padded.
instruction: Given a nonnegative integer documentTokens, a positive integer chunkTokens and a nonnegative overlapTokens smaller than chunkTokens, return the chunk ranges as [{start, end}] with end exclusive. Start at 0 and advance by chunkTokens minus overlapTokens. Clamp the final end to documentTokens and never emit an empty or duplicate range.
hint: Advance by the stride, not by the chunk size, and stop once a start reaches the document length.

tests.label: Overlapping chunks with a short tail
A document shorter than one chunk
An empty document has no chunks
An exact multiple does not emit a trailing empty chunk
